c16.note: The $90B figure is derived, not quoted: 6-7% growth on $84.6B gives about $89.7-90.5B. The Q1 10-Q puts growth at the lower end of that range, so about $89.7B. The 53rd week is confirmed.

c17.note: The 10-Q says sales rose 2.8%, or $596M, to $21.7B. $21,148M plus $596M equals $21,744M, which matches.

c18.note: The 10-Q says it expects sales growth at the lower end of the 6% to 7% range.

c19.note: The FY2026 10-K states growth from $115 million to an all-time high of $84.6B in fiscal 2026. The Q4 release confirms $84.6B.

c20.note: The 10-K states this verbatim. It is background and does not answer the revenue question.

c21.note: U.S. Foodservice FY2026 sales were $58.8B, against company total sales of $84.6B. The claim that some coverage cites the $58.8B figure is not verified, but the segment-versus-total distinction is correct.

c15.note: The release introduces FY2027 guidance of 6%-7% sales growth on a 53-week basis. Applying that to $84.55B gives about $90B, so the B label's roughly $90 billion figure is consistent with the guidance. The release does not state $90B itself.
